description: Everything ENGULA INFO publishes at the user tier, one row per section: how much memory the arena holds, whether the background pipeline keeps up, how close eviction is, whether the last load was clean, and what the engine costs the main thread. Needs no extra exporter flags.

panels.description: Process RSS alongside the two Engula arena totals it contains. `Arena blocks` is the memory allocated for arena blocks; `Live records` is the part of it holding live records. The gap between the two is slack inside the blocks; the gap between `Arena blocks` and RSS is everything outside the arena — server overhead, client buffers and the allocator.
panels.title: Memory Usage

panels.description: The two pressure ratios Engula publishes: `Usage` for memory consumption and `Defrag` for fragmentation. They drive how aggressively reclamation runs — the higher they sit, the more work Engula is doing in the background.
panels.title: Pressure Ratios

panels.description: Arena blocks currently allocated. Read it together with Avg. Block Size: more blocks at a steady average size means the dataset is growing, more blocks at a shrinking average size means fragmentation.
panels.title: Number of Blocks

panels.description: arena_block_bytes / arena_blocks — mean size of an allocated arena block. The divisor is guarded with `> 0`, so the panel stays empty instead of showing NaN when there are no blocks.
panels.title: Avg. Block Size

panels.description: Live records currently held in the arena. This follows the size of the data Engula manages, which is not the same as the Valkey key count.
panels.title: Number of Records

panels.description: arena_record_bytes / arena_records — mean size of a live record, with the same `> 0` divisor guard as Avg. Block Size.
panels.title: Avg. Record Size

panels.description: `Attempted` minus `Created` is what never became a task. `Inline urgent` is the queue being full at creation, `Inline main thread` is the io threads not draining it afterwards — back-pressure versus throughput, so they are not summed.
panels.title: Zip Tasks

panels.description: `Attempted` minus `Created` is what never became a task. `Inline urgent` is the queue being full at creation, `Inline main thread` is the io threads not draining it afterwards — back-pressure versus throughput, so they are not summed. Rezip has no inline-urgent path: a full queue gates creation instead, so `Created` is already the queued count. Its `Attempted` ticks on the 100ms cron whether or not there is anything to do, so read `Created / Attempted` as a hit rate.
panels.title: Rezip Tasks

panels.description: `Attempted` minus `Created` is what never became a task. `Inline urgent` is the queue being full at creation, `Inline main thread` is the io threads not draining it afterwards — back-pressure versus throughput, so they are not summed. Defrag names its two failure reasons, so `Attempted = Created + Threshold + Insufficient`.
panels.title: Defrag Tasks

panels.description: Bytes per second in and out of zip passes. The gap between `Retired` and `Produced` is what this stage gives back.
panels.title: Zip Bytes

panels.description: Bytes per second in and out of rezip passes. The gap between `Retired` and `Produced` is what this stage gives back.
panels.title: Rezip Bytes

panels.description: Bytes per second in and out of defrag passes. The gap between `Retired` and `Produced` is what this stage gives back.
panels.title: Defrag Bytes

panels.description: Work pending in each stage, plus the tasks accepted and not yet finished. Long queues with low in-flight means the pipeline is not picking work up; both high means it is picking it up but not finishing.
panels.title: Queue Lengths

panels.description: `Recyclable` is memory Engula has identified as reclaimable but has not reclaimed yet; `Recycling` is memory currently moving through reclamation. A `Recyclable` line that keeps climbing means reclamation is falling behind.
panels.title: Memory Reclamation

panels.description: How often the eviction timer is armed, and what forced an urgent defragmentation pass. The two urgent lines split by call site, not by caller: `Timer` is evictionTimeProc's spin loop, `Recycle` is performEvictions' tail — a timer tick can raise both.
panels.title: Eviction Activity

panels.description: Records the last RDB load walked. Per-load snapshots, not counters — they can decrease.
panels.title: Records Checked

panels.description: Records the last RDB load discarded. Anything above zero means the logical keyspace changed and a FULLRESYNC was forced — the one alert line in the user tier.
panels.title: Records Dropped

panels.description: Orphaned records cleaned up during the load. Expected behaviour, not an error.
panels.title: Orphans Reclaimed

panels.description: How the last RDB load ran and why. This is the context for reading `Records Dropped`: reason=marker-manual is a deliberate verification reload, totals-dirty is a footer mismatch.
panels.title: Load Mode / Reason

panels.description: Seconds of main-thread time Engula uses per second — the share of the request path the engine costs. This is the only measured time in this section; the scheduler's limits are budgets, not consumption.
panels.title: Main Thread Share

panels.description: Coroutine scheduling rounds per second.
panels.title: Schedule Rate

panels.description: Current coroutine busy level. The reported value is not capped — the scheduler clamps to 10 internally, but this reports what it saw.
panels.title: Busy Level

panels.description: Measured run time divided by scheduling rounds — how long an average round actually takes.
panels.title: Avg. Time per Schedule
